title: Cycle Factors of Regular Graphs via Entropy
authors: Micha Christoph (ETH Zurich, Switzerland), Nemanja  Draganic (University of Oxford, United Kingdom), Antonio Girao (University of Oxford, United Kingdom), Eoin  Hurley  (University of Oxford, United Kingdom), Lukas  Michel (University of Oxford, United Kingdom), Alp Muyesser (University of Oxford, United Kingdom)
abstract: It is a classical result that a random permutation of n elements has, on average, about log n cycles. We generalise this fact to all directed d-regular graphs on n vertices by showing that, on average, a random cycle-factor of such a graph has O((n log d)/d) cycles. This is tight up to the constant factor and improves the best previous bound of the form O(n/ √{log d}) due to Vishnoi. Our results also yield randomised polynomial-time algorithms for finding such a cycle-factor and for finding a tour of length (1 + O((log d)/d))· n if the graph is connected. This makes progress on a conjecture of Magnant and Martin and on a problem studied by Vishnoi and by Feige, Ravi, and Singh. Our proof uses the language of entropy to exploit the fact that the upper and lower bounds on the number of perfect matchings in regular bipartite graphs are extremely close.

   By Theorem 1 and Markov’s inequality, we know that a uni-
formly random cycle-factor of G has at most O((n log d)/d)
cycles with probability at least 1/2. Since σ is almost-
uniform with some error δ, this implies that σ has at most
O((n log d)/d) cycles with probability at least 1/2 − δ. If
we now sample σ independently at least Ω(log n) times and
return the cycle-factor with the least number of cycles, then
the returned cycle-factor has at most O((n log d)/d) cycles
with high probability.
